title: Empirical Evaluation of a Generate–Validate–Repair Loop for Intent→Network Configuration Using a Deterministic Reachability Validator
abstract: We measure the marginal effect of wrapping a single LLM generator (declared gpt-5-mini) with a deterministic reachability validator plus at most one automated repair on intent→device‑configuration tasks. Using a preregistered paired shared‑initial design (cns‑m2026‑01) with N=300 intents (600 episodes), the baseline generator produced execution‑validated correct configurations in 299/300 tasks (99.667%); the guarded pipeline (validator ± one repair) produced 300/300 (100.0%). Paired difference = 0.003333; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap‑percentile CI = [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Provider‑call accounting: 301 model calls (300 generator calls + 1 repair call). All model calls, validator traces, scoring JSON, manifests, and analysis artifacts are archived with SHA‑256 hashes (representative paths and SHAs included in the Disclosure Statement). We interpret the result in light of a near‑ceiling baseline, describe operational implications, enumerate threats to validity, and provide complete reproducibility pointers to the archived run.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are being used to translate operator intent into low‑level device configuration. Production architectures commonly add a deterministic validator (reachability/policy checker) that prevents unsafe proposals from being applied and optionally triggers automated repair. Quantitative, preregistered paired measurements of the marginal effect of such verifier+repair wrappers are rare; similarly, per‑call archival and deterministic reproducibility are uncommon. We executed a fully preregistered paired experiment (cns‑m2026‑01) to measure whether a deterministic reachability validator plus ≤1 automated repair (a GVR loop) increases the rate of correct, safely executable configurations versus the same LLM generator alone. The run archived every model call, provider trace, validator trace, and per‑episode scoring JSON, enabling deterministic reanalysis.
sections.related_work: Work on intent→configuration, verifier‑assisted pipelines, and generate–validate–repair (GVR) architectures motivated our study. Prior engineering and research prototypes report success rates and architectural patterns but often omit preregistered paired inference, per‑call archival, or deterministic reproducibility artifacts. We followed contemporary LLM evaluation best practices: preregistration of estimands and stopping rules; automated contamination and inclusion checks; fixed RNG seeds for selection and bootstrap; and archival of all intermediate artifacts and hashes.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimands: The study preregistration (cns‑m2026‑01) froze the primary estimand (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline), shared‑initial paired design, contamination/exclusion rules, retry policy, repair budget (≤1), confirmatory exact McNemar two‑sided test, and bootstrap CI plan (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). Preregistration SHA‑256: 0726a6c02c1ed6fc379927f4bb0696330f0b00484f15caee5cf4ebc072316bf7.

Task bank and selection: A deterministic pipeline produced the 300 intents by combining filtered public examples and seeded synthetic templates; contamination heuristics (exact string and k‑token shingle overlap) excluded flagged candidates. Final task manifest archived: execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256: 91564bb69ac692e2fbd6321708863d13938309b5433ef1b211541ba5426df990).

Generator, validator, guarded pipeline: Declared generator: gpt‑5‑mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The guarded pipeline invoked deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator v5.0) to parse, simulate, and check intended invariants (allowed_touched_fields, group constraints, no unintended reachability changes). On validator failure the pipeline allowed a single automated repair call. Every model call and validator trace was archived (execution/provider_calls/ and execution/scoring/).

Execution contract and accounting: Preregistered planned_episode_count = 600 (300 intents × shared‑initial reused), maximum_model_calls = 600; automatic retries up to two for transient failures. The actual run completed 600 episodes with zero failures and used 301 model calls (300 generator + 1 repair). Per‑call provider traces and a full call cache are archived (execution/provider_calls/ and execution/call_cache/; a repair trace example: execution/provider_calls/task-000117-guarded-repair.json — SHA‑256: 4deb410d5736ab332cd5caaf00b16051e5b0aef2276255c0770098f63cb523ba).

Scoring and analysis: Episode outcome is binary: 1 = execution‑validated configuration satisfying the intent with no unintended reachability/policy changes as determined by the deterministic validator; 0 otherwise. Primary test: exact McNemar two‑sided on discordant pairs (n10,n01). Complementary uncertainty: bootstrap‑percentile CI on paired difference (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). The analysis executor 'paired_binary_analysis_v1' produced the archived confirmatory outputs (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl — SHA‑256: 7db06f53d650b2ffc5838b392740c75681480829e5db575e44a9a065eadb965e).
sections.results:
Execution and accounting. Planned episodes = 600; completed = 600; failed = 0. Provider calls used = 301 (300 generator calls + 1 repair call). All per‑episode scoring JSONs, provider traces, and call cache entries are archived (execution/scoring/*.json; execution/provider_calls/*.json; execution/call_cache/*).

Aggregates (analysis/condition_summary.csv SHA‑256: 55eacb88c64f29dc...): baseline successes = 299/300 (0.996667); guarded successes = 300/300 (1.0).

Paired contingency and inference (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256: 3421adb52d...): n11=299, n10=1 (baseline=0, guarded=1), n01=0, n00=0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0033333333333332993. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Bootstrap‑percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). The archived contingency CSV and analysis log contain the exact implementation and seeds used so readers can reproduce the p and CI.

Repair and failure diagnostics. Repair‑iteration histogram: 299 tasks required zero repairs; 1 task required a single automated repair (repair trace archived at execution/provider_calls/task-000117-guarded-repair.json — SHA‑256: 4deb410d...). No residual guarded failures remained. Per‑episode scorer JSONs provide failure‑mode annotations (validator violation, parse/syntax, emulator mismatch, specification ambiguity) and are archived under execution/scoring/ for forensic inspection.

Representative artifact examples. Representative episodes (pair‑000001, pair‑000002, pair‑000003) with shared initial proposals and scoring JSONs are archived (execution/responses/task-00000X-shared-initial.txt and execution/scoring/task-00000X-baseline.json/guarded.json). Example: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 = 8f38c8be...) and its baseline/guarded scoring JSON show identical generator outputs for both conditions and the validator's internal parse and simulated final state.
sections.discussion:
Interpretation. The guarded GVR pipeline corrected the single isolated baseline failure at the cost of one additional repair call (provider_calls_used = 301). This shows that a deterministic validator plus a limited repair budget can fix generator mistakes with minimal extra model‑call overhead in a low‑error, controlled emulator corpus. Because the baseline generator already performed near ceiling, the absolute paired improvement is small; in higher base‑error settings the marginal benefit of a validator and repair loop is expected to be larger.

Why exact McNemar p = 1.0. With discordant counts n10=1 and n01=0 the two‑sided exact McNemar enumeration (as implemented in our analysis executor) yields p=1.0. The observed contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv — SHA‑256: 3421adb5...) and the analysis implementation and seeds are archived (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl — SHA‑256: 7db06f53...) so readers can re‑compute alternative exact implementations or one‑sided tests if preferred.

Design choice: shared‑initial semantics. The preregistered shared‑initial design reuses a single generator proposal for both baseline and guarded conditions to isolate the gate’s marginal effect (i.e., the validator±repair decision on the same candidate). This choice improves internal isolation but differs from pipelines that requery the LLM per condition; deterministic_reconciliation.json (analysis artifact SHA‑256: f6da505032ab388ceccda8e85084b53b8cada91a7ccc0dc65601385505f00ea6) documents provider‑call accounting and confirms the single repair call. Users should note the distinction when extrapolating to end‑to‑end systems that may generate different candidates per policy gate.

Operational implications. For systems with already low generator error rates, adding a validator+limited repair yields small absolute gains at small extra cost; where baseline errors or task difficulty are higher, the same architectural pattern can yield larger operational improvement. Design decisions include validator coverage (which properties are checked), repair budget/strategy, latency and cost constraints, and whether to re‑generate candidates when a validator rejects a proposal.

Reproducibility. Every raw response, provider call, validator trace, per‑episode scoring JSON, call cache entry, task manifest, transformation manifest, and analysis output is archived with SHA‑256. Representative SHAs are cited in the Disclosure Statement: execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 176776d1...), execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 91564bb6...), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 3421adb5...), analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 7db06f53...), model config (execution/model_configuration.json — SHA‑256 = a40e96e2...), repair trace (execution/provider_calls/task-000117-guarded-repair.json — SHA‑256 = 4deb410d...). The exact analysis implementation and seeds used for the McNemar test and the bootstrap CI are archived (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl).
sections.conclusion: A preregistered paired shared‑initial experiment (cns‑m2026‑01) with N=300 intents showed baseline success 299/300 and guarded (validator+≤1 repair) success 300/300. The guarded pipeline corrected the single baseline error with a single repair call and 301 total model calls. The small absolute paired improvement reflects a near‑ceiling baseline; for higher baseline error regimes the operational value of a deterministic validator and automated repair is likely larger. All empirical claims are traceable to archived artifacts (paths and SHA‑256 values provided). Future work should evaluate multiple models, iterative repair budgets, and higher‑error real‑world distributions to measure larger marginal effects.

disclosure_statement:
Disclosure Statement — archived provenance and runtime facts

Initial master prompt immutable reference (archived): provenance/master_prompt.txt — SHA‑256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba.

Preregistration: cns‑m2026‑01 (preregistration SHA‑256 = 0726a6c02c1ed6fc379927f4bb0696330f0b00484f15caee5cf4ebc072316bf7). The preregistration froze the research question, estimands, paired shared‑initial design, task selection and contamination rules, maximum repair budget (≤1 repair call per intent), retry policy, confirmatory test (exact McNemar two‑sided), and bootstrap CI plan (10,000 resamples, seed=1729).

Declared LLM and configuration: gpt‑5‑mini as declared generator (execution/model_configuration.json — SHA‑256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The run used the adapter_family 'hosted_netops_gvr_v1'. All model calls and provider traces are archived under execution/provider_calls/ and execution/call_cache/ (full manifest in execution/execution_manifest.json). Provider‑call accounting: hosted_model_call_event_count = 301 (300 generator calls + 1 repair call) as recorded in deterministic_reconciliation.json and the execution manifest.

Orchestration and permitted toolset: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator v5.0) was used to parse candidate configurations, simulate device state transitions in a closed emulator snapshot, check pre‑registered task constraints (allowed_touched_fields, group constraints, preserve_unspecified_state), and produce pass/fail plus structured traces. On validator failure the pipeline allowed a single automated repair call; repair attempts and repair prompts/responses are archived when used (example repair trace: execution/provider_calls/task-000117-guarded-repair.json — SHA‑256: 4deb410d5736ab332cd5caaf00b16051e5b0aef2276255c0770098f63cb523ba).

Reproducibility and archival: every raw response, provider call, validator trace, per‑episode scoring JSON, call cache entry, task manifest, transformation manifest, and analysis output is archived with SHA‑256. Representative artifact SHAs (exact values available in the execution manifest): execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 176776d1c015a652ea2d28ced2be39ffbfec9b969b72ab03e1a1193b567b6dbb), execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 91564bb69ac692e2fbd6321708863d13938309b5433ef1b211541ba5426df990), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA‑256 = 3421adb52d5791a979397368165fc2062e6b9a4a771ce49c0bcac80b02215d55), analysis/analysis_log.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 7db06f53d650b2ffc5838b392740c75681480829e5db575e44a9a065eadb965e), execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 = 8f38c8becd7e1e36d8902e9ba2f09218baad021d77365b20eb52914a4bdf4080), deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA‑256 = f6da505032ab388ceccda8e85084b53b8cada91a7ccc0dc65601385505f00ea6).

Autonomy boundary and human roles: The Research Director selected the broad topic family and approved the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock. After the autonomy lock the AI autonomously performed literature review, study selection, preregistration, code generation, experiment execution, artifact archival, analysis, manuscript drafting, AI‑based peer review, and revision. No manual technical edits, selective rewriting, or post‑lock manual improvement of the manuscript substantive content occurred.

Limitations summary (short): single declared model; closed‑emulator validator proxy for safety; shared‑initial semantics isolates gate marginal effect but does not measure pipelines that requery the LLM per condition; repair budget limited to ≤1 automated repair. Full limitations and per‑artifact references appear in the manuscript body and the archived execution manifest.
limitations: Ceiling baseline: baseline success = 299/300 reduces statistical power to detect larger preregistered improvements.
Task scope and external validity: deterministic emulator‑backed intent corpus; results do not directly generalise to noisy, adversarial, or human‑authored intent distributions in production.
Model scope: single declared model (gpt‑5‑mini); no cross‑model generality claimed.
Validator construct validity: safety operationalized as absence of emulator‑observed unintended reachability changes in a closed‑world snapshot; production safety surfaces may be broader.
Repair budget: only a single automated repair attempt was permitted; iterative multi‑call repair strategies were not evaluated in this confirmatory run.
